clue.text: Undeveloped island connected with old goddess

parts.note: an inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: A remote, undeveloped island linked in legend to some ancient goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is a Scottish word for a small island, found in many place names in the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inchoate is only just begun and not yet fully formed, hence rudimentary.

clue.text: Eastern cooking is the most economical

indicators.note: something cooking is being mixed up and transformed, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eastern cuisine is said to be the cheapest way to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges EASTERN. 'Near' means stingy or mean with money, so the most economical is the nearest.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old sense of stingy or thrifty, so the superlative means the most sparing with money.

clue.text: Song supporting US credit payments

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other, so it comes second

parts.note: honour in its American spelling, credit or esteem given to someone
an aria is a song for a solo voice in an opera

explanation.surface: A tune is used to back up American credit arrangements for payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ARIA below HONOR in the down entry; the American spelling is flagged by 'US'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoraria are fees paid for professional services that nominally need no charge, such as a guest lecture.

clue.text: Skilful side, in trouble over drink

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this piece comes first
the word in places the side letter inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother, as in Much Ado About Nothing
R for right, one side of a stage or a ship
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A clever team gets into a scrape over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the side letter inside the trouble word, and 'over' stacks that above the drink in the down entry. The drink is Italian vermouth, the It of a gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit describes deft handling, a synonym of dexterous or nimble.

clue.text: Irrationally decline to enter a friendly relationship

indicators.note: acting without reason suggests disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly refuses to begin a warm alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrationally' rearranges the fifteen letters of DECLINE TO ENTER A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 agreement of mutual goodwill between Britain and France, and is used for any cordial understanding between nations.

clue.text: "I hold every man a ______ to his profession" (Bacon)

definitions.text: "I hold every man a ______ to his profession" (Bacon)

parts.words: "I hold every man a ______ to his profession" (Bacon)
parts.note: the quotation from Francis Bacon has a word missing, and the solver supplies it from the famous sentence

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a blank after 'a'. The line opens the preface to Bacon's Maxims of the Law: everyone owes their profession something in return.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon's quotation says each person owes a duty to their calling, so the missing word is one who owes.

clue.text: Politician's noisy meeting starts civic row about tradition

parts.note: a demo, short for demonstration, is a loud public protest rally

indicators.note: starts means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A politician's rowdy rally sparks a public argument about custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of civic, row, about and tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, a politician of that party.

clue.text: Interim broadcast stations

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Temporary transmission from radio stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges INTERIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end-of-line railway or bus stations.

clue.text: Give back notes about mounting stage scenery

parts.note: re and te are notes of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: about means the second note goes round the reversed scenery

parts.note: re and te are notes of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising up, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: decor is the scenery and furnishings of a stage set

explanation.surface: Return the musical notes about a stage set rising into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reads the scenery word upwards in this down entry, and 'about' wraps the second note round it. The one word 'notes' supplies two sol-fa syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrocede is to cede back territory, to hand it back to a former owner.

clue.text: Kind behaviour

definitions.meaning: sort or type, as in all kinds of things

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sort, as in 'all manner of things', and also a person's bearing towards others.

clue.text: The private sector returns only half the rubbish

parts.note: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the traditional name for a private in the British army

indicators.note: returns means the chosen letters are read backwards
only half means just the second half of the word sector is kept

explanation.surface: Privatisation pays back only half: what nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps TOR, the back half of SECTOR, and 'returns' turns it to ROT. TOMMY is British slang for a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot is old-fashioned slang for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Pre-Victorian language

definitions.meaning: the period of the four King Georges, 1714 to 1830, just before Victoria
the Kartvelian tongue spoken in the Caucasus republic

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the British era of Georges I to IV, and also the national tongue of the Caucasus state of Georgia.

clue.text: Some typical iconoclastic material

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some conventional image-breaking cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Flyer operating delivery service?

parts.note: a courier or airline seems meant, but the flyer is the bird of folklore said to bring newborn babies

explanation.definitionFit: In nursery folklore a long-legged wading bird delivers babies to their parents.

clue.text: Can be said to be the top value in fur

indicators.note: in places the top value inside the word for fur

parts.note: sable is the costly fur of a small Asian mammal
a peak is the highest point or maximum value

explanation.surface: A claim that the highest price is reached in the fur trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the top value inside the fur; 'value' tempts a price or number reading, but it is a high point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something speakable is able to be uttered, the opposite of unspeakable.

clue.text: Variegated decennial plant

indicators.note: variegated means mixed in colour, so the letters of the next word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A multicoloured plant that blooms once every ten years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variegated' rearranges DECENNIAL. 'Variegated' looks like a description of the plant's leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a yellow-flowered wild plant, either the lesser celandine or the greater.

clue.text: Course supervision

definitions.meaning: a line of travel or heading
management or guidance, as in under the guidance of

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the way something is heading and also the act of managing or guiding people.

clue.text: Model reputation, passed from father to son

parts.note: a last is a shoemaker's wooden model of a foot
a name is one's standing, as in making a name for oneself

explanation.surface: A model's good standing passes down through the family.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAST is the foot-shaped block a cobbler builds a shoe around.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname is the family label inherited down the male line in traditional practice.

clue.text: Tax admitted by former accountant and gold-digger

indicators.note: admitted by means the tax is let inside the other letters

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
CA is a chartered accountant
or is gold in heraldry
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A gold-digger once taken in by a former accountant over tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted by' puts the tax inside the other pieces, between the accountant and the gold. 'gold-digger' reads as one word, but the definition is only 'digger'.
explanation.definitionFit: An excavator is a machine for digging out earth.

clue.text: Traditions that impose duties

definitions.meaning: the government department charging tax on imported goods

explanation.definitionFit: The word means habitual practices, and also the authority that levies charges on goods brought into a country.

clue.text: A hill to get up

parts.note: a rise is a gentle slope or small hill

explanation.surface: A small hill to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to stand up or get out of bed.

clue.text: The group that is wearing goggles

indicators.note: wearing means the specs go round the other letters, as glasses are worn on a face

parts.note: specs, short for spectacles, are glasses
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: The gang are all wearing goggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' wraps the glasses round the abbreviation, as specs sit on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a biological category of related organisms, one class in the classification of life.

clue.text: Tried hard to manipulate voters

indicators.note: to manipulate is to handle and rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician made every effort to manipulate the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulate' rearranges VOTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to make a great effort.

clue.text: King is confronted by destiny

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
met means faced or encountered

explanation.surface: A monarch faces his fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a Turkish-derived word for fate.

clue.text: Sent on a mission to achieve objective

definitions.meaning: posted away from the main body on a special task, as troops are

explanation.definitionFit: Troops sent off on separate duty are posted on detachment, and an unbiased person is aloof and impartial.

clue.text: Uproar in France where boundary fence closes the track

parts.note: BR is British Rail, whose tracks once ran the national network
the French word for where is ou
a ha-ha is a sunken fence or ditch bounding a park

explanation.surface: Trouble in France where a farmer's fence blocks off the lane.
explanation.walkthrough: A HA-HA is a ditch with a wall on one side, used on English country estates to keep livestock out without blocking the view. BR is British Rail, the former national rail operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or fuss.

clue.text: First stage in chasing returned cheque

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes after
returned means the word for cheque is read backwards

parts.note: a giro is a British state benefit cheque

explanation.surface: Early on, pursuing a bounced cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the cheque word backwards and 'chasing' puts 'in' after it. A giro was the cheque in which British unemployment benefit used to be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the beginning or source of something.

clue.text: Right result without guarantee

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for result goes round the other letter

parts.note: to ensue is to follow as a result

explanation.surface: The correct outcome comes without a warranty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside puts ENSUE round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain of something, to secure it.

clue.text: Balance prevents heart leading head

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so this piece is placed first
heart means the middle letters of prevents are taken

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A sense of balance stops the heart from ruling the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the central four letters of PREVENTS, and 'leading' sets them before the headland word. 'heart' and 'head' tempt a heart-versus-head reading of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenness is a state of equilibrium, where both sides weigh the same.
